messages.author: f769d7d2cfcf4edc
messages.subject: Summarizing chains individually?
parts:
Hey everyone,

I'm in the process of converting several latent profile/mixture models to stan by means of marginalizing out the discrete parameters, using simplexes to weight the likelihoods, etc.

Some observations:
1) In JAGS, I often hit the label-switching problem *between* chains, but rarely within (probably due to the conditional sampling method rather than surfing a probability surface for solutions).
2) In Stan, I hit a within-chain label-switching problem. I can solve this by setting constraints (whether it's ordered simplexes or ordered means).

With JAGS, I could visually compare the chains in trace plots and tell obviously that labels were switching, then summarize chains that labeled the same.

With Stan, I can plot each chain's trace separately, but is there an 'easy' way of summarizing a subset of the chains?
That is, if I run a model with 4 chains, is there a way of running summary() on only one of those chains?
I ask because in one model, 2 chains converge to the "correct" mixture and 2 chains definitely do not, and I would like to summarize each chain separately.

A hacky solution is to use coda: coda::summary(As.mcmc.list(stan.out)[[1]])

Is there a more elegant solution using rstan's tools?

messages.author: f769d7d2cfcf4edc
messages.subject: Re: Summarizing chains individually?
parts:
Because I know we all love code examples:

x1 <- rnorm(100)
x2 <- rnorm(50,5,3)
x <- c(x1,x2)

mixed.stan <- "
data {
    int N;
    vector[N] y;
    int K;
}

parameters {
    simplex[K] theta[N]; //Probability of belonging to each ~N
    vector[K] mu; // means of each ~N
  //Ordered mean constraint
  // This works considerably better than a simplex order constraint
  // n_eff is larger, and alpha/alpha_s is computed correctly
  //real mu_1;
  //real<lower=mu_1> mu_2;
    vector<lower=0>[K] sigma;
    //simplex[K] alpha;
  //Ordered simplex (alpha) constraint
  // Use K-length positive ordered vector as constraint, then softmax to produce parameter of interest
  positive_ordered[K] alpha;
}
transformed parameters {
  simplex[K] alpha_s;
  alpha_s <- softmax(alpha);
  //vector[2] mu;
  //mu[1] <- mu_1;
  //mu[2] <- mu_2;
}
model {
    real ps[K]; //tmp variable for holding log probs of each mixture component
    mu ~ normal(0,3);
    sigma ~ cauchy(0,3);
    for(i in 1:N){
        //theta[i] ~ dirichlet(rep_vector(1.0,K));
        theta[i] ~ dirichlet(alpha_s);
    }

    //Likelihood
    for(i in 1:N){
        for(k in 1:K){
            ps[k] <- log(theta[i,k]) + normal_log(y[i],mu[k],sigma[k]);
        }
        increment_log_prob(log_sum_exp(ps));
    }
}

"

stanOutMixed <- stan(model_code = mixed.stan,data = list(y=x,K=2,N=150),iter=10000,chains = 4)

messages.author: fc5d3270037d7478
messages.subject: Re: Summarizing chains individually?
parts:
I wasn't at the right computer before, but I just double checked now and if you do 

s <- summary(stanfit)

then s should have an element named summary (all chains combined) and c_summary (chains separately).

messages.author: f769d7d2cfcf4edc
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Re: Summarizing chains individually?
parts: Indeed! Thank you. I should've read the docs better. I'm not used to the S4 world, so I didn't think to look in the methods docs.

I wasn't at the right computer before, but I just double checked now and if you do 

s <- summary(stanfit)

then s should have an element named summary (all chains combined) and c_summary (chains separately).

messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Summarizing chains individually?
parts:
It's better for Stan to identify the model if you can.

If you can't, you could just go directly to computing inferences
for quantities of interest, which very often won't depend
on the labels. Unfortunately, this can potentially mask
non-convergences that would be detected otherwise.

- Bob

messages.author: f769d7d2cfcf4edc
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Summarizing chains individually?
parts:
In some models, it won't matter which label is which.

In this model, the parameter of interest does depend on labels.

The issue in this particular model, actually, is that different chains are converging on different solutions.

Using PPC, both solutions actually do appear to be good fits.

The true values are as follows:
K = 2, mu[1] = 0, mu[2] = 5, sd[1] = 1, sd[2] = 3, alpha[1] = .66, alpha[2] = .33 (where alpha is the mixing proportion).
One solution is very close to the true parameters.

The other solution is basically mu[1] and mu[2] = 0, sd[1] = 1, sd[2] = 6.
Both of the map decently well onto the observed density. N(0,1) takes care of the heavier density near 0, and N(0,6)'s upper tail essentially covers the second cluster's density.

I'm not sure how to change the model to converge on only the correct solution.
I could probably make the prior of sd[2] smaller.

Edit:
I'll add that I've had similar experiences using other cluster modeling packages.
In a similar dataset, Mclust found the correct solution, but flexmix found a solution akin to the second I mentioned, where the means are equal, but the second group's distribution is much, much wider.
